rule: Venue-specific abstract projection only. QG1/QG2 are claim-preserving compressions of their canonical cited masters. Q1 may additionally mention the executed R11 algorithmic theorem only when the separate result-bound TQE projection verifier confirms the live R11 result, protocol and authority boundary before PDF generation.

Q1.allowed: algorithmic theorem for the frozen R6M six-slot grammar and declared objective

abstracts.Q1: TARE block encoding exposes auxiliary anticommuting frames and non-unique Tag choices, but those donor-owned freedoms do not determine how much frame support an exact optimum can intrinsically require. We study a frozen three-block shared-Tag TARE-M2 grammar under a declared support-count objective. Exact counterexamples first show that natural weight-one joint families are incomplete: a split-anchor construction improves cost 9 to 8, and a frame-for-Tag borrow improves 6 to 5. The central all-size exchange theorem then proves that every admitted instance has an exact optimum with frame support at most two, while later counterexamples show that no small named support-two taxonomy should be promoted to a universal closed form. A prospectively frozen executable follow-up exploits this theorem to generate legal ordered support-two anticommuting pairs directly and validates a direct exact solver with O(n^9) search time after O(n) preprocessing for the frozen six-slot grammar. This algorithmic claim is independently checked on finite pair counts and exact panels, but it is not a production-runtime, hardware-resource, or generic TARE complexity claim. The result is a sharp expressivity and exact-algorithm study over donor-exposed compilation choices under one explicitly bounded objective.
abstracts.QG1: Algorithm selection and Instance Space Analysis already describe regions in which methods perform well. We ask what additional exact objects can be recorded when a quantum-compilation family admits constructive witnesses, exact referees, and machine-checked bounds. We call the resulting record a compilation regime geometry and separate intrinsic support, proof-derived search ceilings, objective-indexed certificate validity, boundary representability, named trade mechanisms, and prospective falsification. Across several exact compiler models, these coordinates behave differently. In shared-Tag R6M TARE, an all-size theorem bounds exact optima to frame support at most two while exact counterexamples repeatedly refute smaller named support-two taxonomies. In a distinct R6I rank-2 grammar, whole-system normalization proves the tight intrinsic value one, whereas a production conserved-syndrome proof gives a safe but looser ceiling of five. A separate theorem identifies a cost-weight cone where the support-one certificate remains valid. SixLCU has a theorem-grade simple exactness boundary on its exhaustive small domain. StabPrep instead refutes a prospectively frozen forecast and exhibits mixed feature cells, proving that the frozen 13-feature vocabulary cannot perfectly determine donor exactness. These cases do not establish a universal phase diagram. They show why exact compiler studies should report multiple authority-bearing coordinates rather than collapse theorem, proof ceiling, feature classifier, and forecast into one performance map.
abstracts.QG2: Static quantum-cost analysis and resource estimation are established; we study a narrower authority question in a frozen shared-Tag TARE compilation family with an unrestricted exact dynamic-programming referee. A static forecaster mixes explicit feasible constructions, theorem-backed exactness, finite-domain equalities, and unverified predictions. We ask which of these statements survives an exact counterexample. The initial forecaster evaluates three feasible subfamilies without calling the unrestricted referee. Across 9,546 registered compared instances it agrees on 9,545 and fails on one prospectively generated three-qubit case, where the exact optimum is 10 while all three closed-form terms return 11. That single row refutes universal closed-form exactness, so aggregate accuracy is not the headline. Two stronger layers remain valid: the returned construction still certifies an upper bound, and an independent all-size theorem still places an exact optimum inside the full support-two family. The witness localizes the failed layer to an omitted out-of-own-target-support borrow. A separately frozen successor admits that mechanism, while theorem-backed forecaster F2 computes the exact support-two family minimum without the unrestricted referee. Later counterexamples further refine smaller named families without weakening F2. The contribution is a refutation-localization-repair study and ForecastCertificate reporting hierarchy that keeps feasible bounds, theorem-backed exact family minima, finite hypotheses, and forecast-only rows scientifically distinct.
